Per tick compute jerk=|F_j-2*F_{j-1}+F_{j-2}| on last 4 commanded force magnitudes; if >0.618, retract 3cm for 4 ticks with KP*0.3, resume at same arclength. Physical 20/20 PyBullet DIRECT, friction 0.05-0.80, trochoid path, compare env AEGIS_GATE=inloop. Fixture_B: with_gate=1.00/without=0.00 (Fisher p=1.45e-11); Fixture_R: with_gate=0.95/without=0.20 (Welch p=2.2e-06); Fixture_A: with_gate=1.00/without=0.75. 352 vetoes across 60 gate-on episodes. metrics.mechanism: Planner only (no gate, no controller, no admission logic). The champion trochoid superimposes a circular scrub loop of amplitude amp=TROCHOID_R_M=0.015 m whose phase w = s*rate advances monotonically along the whole path (rate = DR/R = 33.33 rad/m). I17 negates the winding on odd rows. Implemented as a SIGNED ACCUMULATOR w += rate*ds*sign(row), NOT as a phase negation: literally negating w on odd rows would jump the tool offset by up to 2*amp = 0.03 m at every row turn, which is a teleport (G7), not a path. AEGIS_TROCH_ALT<=0 keeps the champion expression s*DR/R verbatim, so the default rig is bit-identical.

prereg_bar.goal: cancel the per-row lateral residual that a same-winding loop imposes

mechanism_proof.statement: w becomes a TRIANGLE wave (row 0: 0->W, row 1: W->0, W=rate*row_length=13.33 rad=2.12 turns). The offset locus is a function of w alone, so row 1's loop trace equals row 0's EXACTLY (max deviation 0.0 m) - it retraces instead of advancing to a fresh phase.

metrics.falsification: No lateral drift existed to cancel: the champion's per-row mean v-offset is -0.0022 / +0.0017 m, already ~0 against a 0.015 m loop amplitude, so the hypothesis that same-winding loops bias the path laterally is FALSE as stated. Worse, the fix is strictly destructive. Making w a triangle wave removes the ONLY thing that makes the superimposed loops add footprint - a fresh phase per row - so on a 2-row patch half the rows re-walk an already-swept trace. Slip is bit-identical (0.0106 m both arms) and there are no escapes, so this is purely a footprint loss: fixture_B coverage_cont -0.0609 (Welch p=4.8e-05) and success 20/20 -> 6/20 (Fisher p=3.3e-06); fixture_R 19/20 -> 8/20 (Fisher p=4.3e-04); fixture_A coverage_cont flat (-0.0015, p=0.88) but success 20/20 -> 14/20 (Fisher p=0.020) because with 3 rows the third row repeats row 0 and pushes episodes across the 0.90 threshold. metrics.class_level: Drift-cancelling winding is falsified for C1 loop-superimposed scrub paths: winding reversal is only C1 if the phase is made continuous, and a continuous phase is necessarily a retrace, which costs more footprint than the drift it removes. metrics.root_cause: The I21 spec premise ('fitted got B 0.20 vs trochoid 1.00') is STALE: it describes the v1 `fitted` of commit ac8bc4b, not the path the rig ships. v1 is reconstructed verbatim in closed form and scored with the rig's own fine-cell kernel (_coverage_cont: fine pitch 0.025 m, cell covered iff a contact lies within r_eff of the centre), so the loss is ATTRIBUTED, not asserted. On fixture-B, v1 emitted ONE row: v_start = -side/2 + r_eff = -0.025, v_end = +side/2 - r_eff = +0.025, pitch p = 2*r_eff*0.8 = 0.056, so the while-loop places v=-0.025 and then stops at v=+0.031 > v_end. One row dilated by r_eff=0.035 spans 0.070 m of the 0.120 m patch, and the u-axis inset (-half+r_eff .. +half-r_eff) additionally shaves the two u end columns. Analytic ceiling of v1 verbatim: fixture_B 0.8021, fixture_A 0.9306 -- and 100.00% of the missed fine cells are RIM cells on every suite x tool cell (rim/interior miss split = 1.00/0.00), which is the signature of a band that does not SPAN, not of an interior pitch stripe and not of a phase bug. Marginal recovery of each single change, fixture-B ceiling: remove the u-inset only -> 0.8333 (+0.0312); make the row walk span the inset sub-rect only -> 0.8125 (+0.0104); both -> 0.8333; the shipped v2 rule n = ceil(side/(2*r_eff)) rows placed at the band centres with NO inset -> 1.0000 (+0.1979, 2 rows, pitch 0.060 m). Verdict on the spec's three hypotheses: (a) pitch math -- YES, the row plan never spanned the patch; (b) inset -- secondary, +0.0312 on B and only because it double-counts a footprint the scoring kernel already applies; (c) phase bug -- REFUTED, no interior miss exists in any variant.
metrics.class_level: The defect is a class, not an instance: any footprint-aware pitch plan parameterised by an INSET sub-rect inherits it, because the scorer already inflates every contact by r_eff, so the plan must span the PATCH at pitch <= 2*r_eff with no inset. That is exactly the v2 rule and it is what ships. Nothing further is left to fix in the pitch, so I10 closes WITH a cause rather than open-ended.
metrics.champion_ceiling: The same kernel run on the champion: trochoid's analytic ceiling is 0.9219 / 0.9531 / 1.0000 on fixture-B for the three pads (mean 0.9583) and 100% of ITS misses are also rim cells. The champion clears the 0.90 gate only because pad 2's footprint is large enough to cover the rim; pads 0 and 1 cannot reach 1.0 on geometry alone. `fitted` reaches 1.0000 on all six suite x tool cells, so the physics run confirms the head realises the ceiling exactly rather than adding any recovery.
metrics.success_caveat: At pose_noise 0,0 BOTH arms are already saturated at 20/20, so the Fisher p on success is 1.0 and the whole signal is coverage_cont. The success-margin claim for `fitted` therefore rests on the earlier 20-seed paired decider at the rig's nominal planning error (run 165 / run 170, AEGIS_POSE_NOISE=0.01,2: fitted B 0.875 vs trochoid B 0.750), which is cited here as prior evidence, NOT re-claimed from this run.
metrics.honest_caveats: (1) `path_len_m` is logged from scrub_uv(spec, mode) with the DEFAULT r_eff=0.035, not the pad's own r_eff, so on fixture-A pad 2 the logged length (1.3878 m) overstates the commanded path (0.9409 m) and the step budget therefore gives that one arm ~2.2x the intended speed. On fixture-B all three pads plan the identical 2-row path (0.8939 m), so the G2 metric carries no such confound. Left unedited: path_len_m is a log-only field, it touches no scored quantity, and changing the step budget would silently re-time every other idea's episodes. (2) fixture-A pad 2 is the only cell where the two are not identical, and it is 1.0000 there anyway. (3) The rig's documented limits stand: force-driven pad with no arm, flat top faces, normal force ~0.5 N in rig units, Tier-4 gate is a post-hoc tag.

metrics.root_cause: The trigger is a UNITS MISMATCH and is therefore inert exactly where the rig scores. GATE_MAX_JERK=0.618 is the Tier-4 threshold for the EPISODE statistic jerk_proxy = mean_t(||F_t - 2F_{t-1} + F_{t-2}||^2) -- a mean of SQUARED vector second differences, which the champion scores at 0.0028-0.0098 with a max of 0.0200 over all 120 episodes. The in-loop trigger instead tests a PER-TICK absolute second difference of the commanded force MAGNITUDE in newtons on a 3.0 N clamped command. Measured per-tick max 0.671-4.741 N, all of it from the pre-contact approach ramp (0 -> rail); inside the scrub the commanded force is ~30x below the threshold forever. Result: across 120 candidate episodes (2 noise x 3 suites x 20 seeds) and 190 vetoes, ZERO fired in the scrub phase and ZERO while the tool was in contact, so no response to this signal can touch the swept patch.
metrics.scored_effect: 0.0000 coverage_cont delta on all three suites at BOTH conditions (Welch p=1.0, Fisher p=1.0, keep=false). metrics.falsification: I3 IS FALSIFIED AS LEARNING, NOT MERELY UNVALIDATED. Three independent measurements say the same thing. (1) The deployed action is a constant: 97.6% of its own mean over 2e4 plausible observations, with E dv = 0.77 of a quantity the planner can compute in closed form. (2) A zero-parameter constant at that closed-form value beats the net on every suite at both noise conditions, so no part of the net's performance needs the net. (3) The I3 spec's own pre-registered bar is not met: 'R success under noise >= 0.95, Fisher p < 0.01' gives R 0.95 (19/20) at Fisher p = 0.043596, and 6 discordant fail->success pairs cannot reach p < 0.01 at 20 seeds (5 give 0.047124, 7 give 0.008316) -- the constant cleared 7 and reached 0.008316. Independently, the 2026-09-28 SEGMENT+METRIC FREEZE bans any learned/adaptive variant from a keep, so I3 could not have been scored keep even had the net won.
metrics.class_level: Two closures. (a) A residual policy on a force-driven plan can only return the plan's own constants; a planner defect that is expressible in closed form must be fixed in the planner, because a policy that has to rediscover it pays 6405 parameters, a training run and a stochastic decider to land 77% of the way to a number the geometry already determines. (b) The champion's row-anchor defect is a general PLANNER class, not a fixture-B quirk: any path built as [v0 + r*CELL_M] from v0 = -side/2 is off-centre by exactly CELL_M/2 in v for every patch size, so the fix is one term in the row list.

metrics.lane: latency / edge budget (local RTX 3050 fp16, canonical CPU rig for the G4 paired record)
metrics.variant: I4 1-NFE shortcut action expert (Frans et al. arXiv:2410.12557 shortcut model, or MeanFlow arXiv:2505.13447) replacing the 10-step flow-matching loop, to bring the chunk from 285 ms to <=25 ms on a Jetson Orin Nano. Step A is the pre-registered local pre-check: split the chunk into VLM-prefix vs expert-step before booking any Colab time.
metrics.law: t_chunk(N) = t_prefix + t_unattr + N*t_expert, with t_prefix and t_unattr paid ONCE per chunk (KV cache filled once, action chunk produced once) and t_expert linear in the NFE count (equations I4.1). The admissible NFE count is N* = (25 - t_prefix - t_unattr)/t_expert (I4.2).
metrics.measured_split_2cam_512: t_prefix 54.87 ms + t_unattr 16.13 ms + N*11.40 ms. Decomposition closes to 0.01 ms: 54.87+16.13+10*11.40 = 185.0 vs 184.99 measured; amortised 10*114.0/10 = 11.40 vs directly measured 1-step 11.50. Timed by wrapping the two REAL methods (embed_prefix, denoise_step) inside the shipped sample_actions, not by a reconstruction.
metrics.falsifier_triggered: I4 pre-registered success bar = 1-NFE chunk <= 25 ms AND action MSE <= 1.2x the 10-step MSE. MEASURED 1-NFE = 82.09 ms (3.28x the budget). N* = (25-71.00)/11.40 = -4.04, NEGATIVE: the fixed cost alone is 2.84x the budget at N=0, so the bar is unreachable for EVERY NFE count including zero. Reachable at any N: false. Triggered BEFORE training, so the MSE half was never spent.
metrics.prediction_where_1nfe_lands: 82.40 ms predicted by (I4.1) vs 82.09 ms measured — 0.4% error. The measurement is self-consistent with the law, so the falsifier is arithmetic, not a measurement artefact.
metrics.cause_not_the_sampler: Of the 82.09 ms surviving 1-NFE, 71.00 ms (86.5%) is spent before the first action vector exists and 11.40 ms (13.9%) is the denoiser the shortcut model would shorten. Eliminating the loop ENTIRELY is worth 2.25x (184.99 -> 82.09 ms) and still misses by 3.28x. t_prefix is linear in image tokens at 0.855 ms/token (177 tok -> 54.87 ms; 113 tok -> 27.71 ms) while t_expert does not depend on camera count at all. The lever is the conditioning-token count, not the NFE count.
metrics.one_camera_floor: 1-cam 512: t_prefix 27.71 + t_unattr 15.40 = 43.11 ms fixed, N* = -1.59, still 1.72x the budget at N=0. 1-NFE measured 59.40 ms. Dropping a camera halves the prefix (177 -> 113 tokens) and is the only intervention that moved it, but not far enough.
metrics.negative_result_resolution_knob_inert: resize_imgs_with_padding 512 -> 256 did NOT reduce the token count (177 in both arms; the ckpt preprocessor owns the resize and the model-side override does not reach it) and did NOT reduce latency: 2-cam 190.20 ms at 256 vs 185.29 at 512; 1-cam 235.30 at 256 vs 157.39 at 512. A free 4x on the prefix is NOT available from this config, and any future edge plan that assumes it must first move the resize into the graph.

metrics.class_level: Latency budgets can be unreachable for reasons orthogonal to the optimisation variable. Here the NFE count was never binding: a fixed per-chunk cost (prefix + preprocessing, 71.00 ms) overshoots the 25 ms target on its own. Shortcut/one-step samplers are the standard answer to flow-matching latency, and they are the wrong lever whenever the fixed cost dominates. This is I18/I22 in reverse: there a plan was limited by a representation rather than a policy, here a budget is limited by a representation rather than a function-evaluation count.
metrics.honest_cost: The 2.25x from deleting the flow loop is real and bankable on its own terms, but it does not reach the product target; anyone citing I4 for latency must cite 82.09 ms, not 25 ms. The A2/A3 runs are noisier than A (1-cam 10-step spread 190-310 ms across 15 timed chunks) because the 1-camera batch rebuilds the policy per case; the prefix medians (27.71/27.88) are stable and are the numbers the conclusion rests on, the totals are not used for any claim.
metrics.predictions_refuted: I4 assumed the 285 ms figure was dominated by the 10-step loop, so 1-NFE would land near 29 ms. MEASURED 82.09 ms. The loop was 113.99/184.99 = 61.6% of the chunk, not the whole story: 29.7% is the prefix and 8.7% is per-chunk preprocessing that no sampler change touches.
metrics.frontier_after: I4 closes as a SAMPLER question. It re-opens as a PREFIX question: the latency frontier is conditioning-token count per chunk (0.855 ms/image token, paid once per chunk, 86.5% of the surviving 1-NFE time), not NFE count. Interventions that follow from the measurement, in order: (a) cache the prefix across chunks instead of recomputing it (the KV cache is already built, then thrown away 50 steps later); (b) fewer image tokens per camera / one camera; (c) a smaller VLM trunk. None of these is a queued idea and none is executable in the CPU rig, so no next run is claimed. I4 stays discarded; the champion trochoid+ROW_CENTRE=1 stays frozen at fixture_B 1.0.

novelty_check: Negative result with no prior-art conflict. pi0.7 (arXiv:2604.15483) claims diverse-context conditioning including strategy/episode metadata; RoboTTT (arXiv:2607.15275) argues test-time training is brittle, which predicts exactly this outcome (an untrained tag is a prompt, not a channel). Our claim is the first paired null-control measurement OF that conditioning at edge scale: action-space distance separates a success tag from a failure tag by 64.8% of the observation scale while a synonym of the same word recovers 90% of that distance. No keep is claimed.
falsifier: I6's own abort rule is NOT triggered, and this is logged rather than buried: the tag is genuinely not ignored (2.93 vs a 1e-3 threshold). The mechanism fails its ADDED controls instead - synonym 44%/90%, position 46%, whole-instruction swap 64%, direction cosine p 0.585.
root_cause: The FT expert was never trained on quality/failure-metadata tokens, so the tag is an out-of-distribution token sequence that perturbs the 16-layer prefix KV cache. Magnitude tracks perturbation, not meaning; the flow expert has no learned mapping from tag semantics to action.
verdict: DISCARD. Not because the tag is ignored (it is not) but because a channel whose effect is indistinguishable from replacing SUCCESS with PASS cannot certify a quality-conditioned policy. The honest positive: the language prefix is padded to 48 tokens for every arm at 4-15 real tokens with flat 2.6% latency spread, so metadata conditioning is free and the I4 latency frontier is entirely image tokens. G7-clean, seg 15, transfer_success metric, zero teleport, zero rig edit.

math_verdict.implicit_action: a* = -(I+Q)^{-1} b, a minimum only for Q > 0
math_verdict.affine_collapse: E affine in a implies a = -b(s,F), rank(grad_a grad_a E) = 0, an action-independent vector field (matches the I19.5/I20 measured-inert trigger)
math_verdict.warp_dichotomy: for E = ||F_SE3||^2 + lambda*pen and E = ||s-s_contact||^2/(2 sigma^2) + lambda*||F_SE3||, grad_M E is constant, hence a rigid translation, hence the induced metric g = dT^T dT and the affordance structure are unchanged; any F-dependence that did change g is non-conservative and hence not an energy
math_verdict.flow_bridge_fatal: div_a(-grad_a E) = -trace(Q) < 0 contracts Lebesgue measure; flow matching requires a mass-preserving v under the continuity equation d_sigma rho + div(rho v) = 0; the bridge is broken at step 1 and collapses to HMC/Langevin energy sampling

metrics.mechanism: N191 refuted every estimator variable and attributed the pose-noise floor to the ray window's CONTAINMENT of the top face (N190.3). Widening H is closed (H=0.9 loses to H=0.6, N190.6). N192 therefore changes the SENSOR: a k x k lattice of +-H windows at pitch d = 1.5a (a = H - hypot(0.34,0.14) = 0.2323 m = the inf-norm containment slack), whose union covers the plausible-centre set (half-extent 3 sigma), keeping only the ONE cast that best contains the face. The containing cast is identified by its TOP-POINT COUNT (maximal exactly when the window holds the whole face; 123 points = the full-face grid count); ties go to the cast nearest the prior, so k=1 is the frozen code path bit-identically. A containing cast's point set is UNTRUNCATED, so the frozen mean estimator and the frozen PCA yaw are reused verbatim and the N190.3 truncation-bias term is identically zero for the selected cast. k = ceil(4 sigma / a) + 1 -> 6 (36 casts) at 0.24/0.28 m, 7 (49) at 0.32 m, 1 (frozen, bit-identical) while sigma <= a.

hypothesis: The cast lattice's k^2 casts exist only to answer a k^2-way argmax, yet N192 cast every candidate at the full n x n resolution, so the sensor paid k^2 n^2 rays to keep one cast's points; and k was derived from a alone (ceil(4 sigma/a)+1) although the only real constraint is the covering radius d/2 <= a, so the shipped d = 1.5a is 1.78x the rays of the tightest legal pitch d = 2a. Buying both back must be FREE in coverage.

mechanism.N195.1_containment_set: a window at offset o holds the WHOLE top face iff max(|f-o|_inf) <= a = H - rho_inf = 0.2323 m, so the offsets that work are the square C(f) = f + [-a,a]^2. A lattice L(d) of pitch d and half-extent (k-1)d/2 hits C(f) for every |e|_inf <= E iff d/2 <= a AND (k-1)d/2 >= E, i.e. k = ceil(2E/d)+1 at fixed E = 3 sigma. N192's k = ceil(4 sigma/a)+1 is exactly this at d = 1.5a and is a d-LAW: the shipped k is the minimum for its own pitch and 1.78x the count of the tightest legal pitch d = 2a. Re-deriving k from d leaves the shipped expression EXACT (ceil(6 sigma/(1.5a))+1 = ceil(4 sigma/a)+1) and makes the budget a knob.
mechanism.N195.2_coarse_to_fine: the argmax score is the BORDER MARGIN m(o) = min over the four sides of the gap between the top-point bbox and the window border, not the point count. m >= 0 iff the window contains the face and m <= a - max|f-o|; it is a DISTANCE, hence it survives a coarse grid as long as the coarse pitch 2H/(n_c-1) < a.
mechanism.N195.3_count_criterion_REFUTED: the point count ALIASES on a coarse grid. Measured at 0.64,128 with the count score, n_c=8 (pitch 171 mm) picked a CUT window (32 top points instead of the full-face 123) and doubled reg_err_xy (43.2 vs 1.9 mm on seed 91002); n_c=16 left a count margin of 0 on 1 of 3 seeds, i.e. the coarse grid could not separate the candidates at all. With the border-margin score the same n_c=8 still failed once in 8 (reg_err_xy max 253 mm, 32 points) while n_c=12 (pitch 109 mm = 0.47a) and n_c=16 (80 mm = 0.34a) were identical and clean (err med 6.55, max 16.95 mm). Measured threshold: the coarse pitch must be below ~0.5 a_slack; shipped n_c = 16.

description: N207 SOLVER-RATE CONVERGENCE. Category: rig validity / numerical verification -- a frontier un-attacked in runs 1-355, chosen because the queue was empty since run 309 and the last two iterations produced no new state. All 355 prior runs used exactly ONE integrator setting (240 Hz, 12 substeps per 20 Hz control tick); the rig header itself records the contact stability number sqrt(CONTACT_K/m)*dt = 0.466 at 240 Hz, i.e. UNDER HALF the explicit limit, so the certified fixture_B 1.00 had never been refined. New knob AEGIS_SIM_HZ (default 240, byte-identical) changes ONLY setTimeStep and the substep count per tick; the 20 Hz control tick, commanded arclength speed, phase labels, press law and tick budget are identical at every rate. Sweep 120/240/480/960/1920 Hz x 20 seeds x {A,B,R}, each rate paired in-rig against the frozen 240 Hz champion on the SAME seeds. RESULT 1 (VALIDATES the standing certification): coverage_cont is solver-independent -- an 8x rate range moves it by <1e-3 on all three suites with success 20/20 everywhere, and a non-saturated control (raster at pose noise 0.03,6, where A=0.9396/15-20 and R=0.9289/13-20) reproduces to 0.9391/15-20 and 0.9289/13-20. The champion B=1.00 does not rest on the discretisation; N197/N199 stand. RESULT 2 (FALSIFIES a prior result in this segment): force_compliance is NOT converged at 240 Hz -- strictly monotone in the rate (A 0.3060->0.9012, R 0.6927->0.9539), Richardson order ~1.0/~1.25, 240 Hz sitting -0.415 (A) and -0.199 (R) below the limit. The pooled 25.3% force-violation rate and every force reading built on it (N202.2, N202.4, N205.2-N205.4 magnitudes) are therefore measured at an unconverged operating point and are RETIRED as force evidence; the DIRECTION of N205.4 survives. RESULT 3 (mechanism): under-resolved contact rings -- fn_std falls >2x with the rate while fn_mean rises to within 0.02 N of the 0.5 N setpoint, so the 240 Hz head under-presses and overshoots the band. RESULT 4 (why it was invisible): fixture_B is dead flat (fn_std 0.0089, force_compliance 1.0 at EVERY rate) and the G4 bar reads B -- every force result in this segment is measured on the one suite where the integrator does not matter and reported from the one where the metric has no dynamic range; the force axis has no usable dynamic range at any rate. METHODOLOGY: the knob was first written with a default argument, so --compare-env was silently inert and produced a plausible keep=true Welch 1.07e-05 on a fake fixture_A covc of 0.3625; the artifact was deleted rather than logged, and the audit script now asserts bit-identity of the paired arm.

description: N208 separates N207's two indistinguishable causes for the force non-convergence. The solver ITERATION budget was the bare literal 80 in all of runs 1-356, so the residual was either the integration RATE or the ITERATION count. A new knob AEGIS_SOLVER_ITERS (default 80 = frozen, call-time read, orthogonal to SIM_HZ) settles it: 4x and 16x the iterations at a fixed 240 Hz are EPISODE-IDENTICAL on every tracked channel with unchanged wall clock, and 960 Hz at 16x iterations reproduces 960 Hz at 80 -- the non-convergence is entirely explicit-integration ringing, with NO free recovery knob and a 3.9x wall-clock price for convergence. A positive control proves the parameter is live (1 pass differs by 2.44e-04 m) and that this 2-body contact converges by 8 passes, so 80 was already 10x converged. Two further results: 3840 Hz shows 1920 Hz was NOT the asymptote N207 called it (A 0.9012->0.9334, R 0.9539->0.9713, order ~0.90, no arm flat), and the force deltas N207 retired were largely discretisation error that CONVERGES TO ZERO -- every N205 contrast shrinks 1.5-23.3x and loses significance, with coverage_cont as the control that does not shrink. coverage_cont is solver-independent over the full 2D dose, so the champion's B = 1.00 does not rest on any axis of the discretisation this rig can vary. Validity audit, new_mechanism=false, no keep claimed on the primary metric.

summary: Validity audit (new_mechanism=false) of the rig's POSE-NOISE-OFFSET axis. Every labelled pose-noise level in runs 1-361 is a mixture over realized offsets spanning 0..3.63 sigma from n=20 unbounded Gaussian draws, so the offset that moves coverage_cont had never been held at a controlled magnitude. Two frozen-default plan-frame knobs (AEGIS_POSE_FIX_U/V) turn the axis into a controlled dose: 21 held-offset arms + 3 stochastic levels at 100 seeds, 21 arms paired in-rig on the SAME 20 seeds. P1 CONFIRMED (realized max 3.63x the labelled sigma at all three levels). P2 CONFIRMED inside the coverage regime: over 600 episodes with |offset|<=0.08 m, ZERO escapes, ZERO stall, ZERO z-excursion, max |d slip_m| 1.8e-4 m -- a held offset is a PLAN-FRAME error, and the slip channel the segment's mechanism rests on is dead here. The escape boundary is closed-form exact on 6 (suite,axis,sign) cells and on fixture_R it splits by FACE TYPE, not by suite (v=+0.12: 0/9 round vs 11/11 elongated) -- 4/4 as predicted. title: N214-PAD-FOOTPRINT-AXIS: validity audit of the TOOL BODY -- the head's footprint and mass are two unvaried floors, and the frozen certificate sits 1.27x and 1.45x above them
summary: Validity audit (new_mechanism=false) of the rig's TOOL-BODY axis, the last unvaried term after N207 rate, N208 iterations, N209 friction, N210 force, N211 kernel, N212 dose and N213 pose-noise. In runs 1-362 the head changed only through tool_id = seed % 3, which moves the footprint (r_eff 0.035/0.040/0.050), the mass (0.080/0.105/0.092 kg) and the thickness (0.012/0.030/0.006 m) together and aliases them with the seed, so the head had never been a controlled dose -- while r_eff is the term every coverage law in the segment is written in (the N211 kernel dilation, the N212 frontier s <= 0.486*2 r_eff, the 'raster failures = tool 0 (r_eff 3.5 cm) only' claim). Three absolute diagnostic knobs (AEGIS_PAD_HU_M / AEGIS_PAD_HV_M / AEGIS_PAD_MASS, all default 0.0 = the frozen per-tool value; in-plane extents and body mass only, thickness/press/path/scoring kernel untouched) turn the head into a controlled dose: 35 arms, 2100 episodes, every arm paired in-rig on the SAME 20 seeds, identity arm bit-identical to Run350 (60/60 on coverage_cont/success, in-rig baseline included). TWO FLOORS found, on two different channels. COVERAGE floor: coverage_cont = 1.0000 and 20/20 for every r_eff >= 0.0275 m, 0.9062 (= 29/32 cells) at 0.025, 0.6414 / 0-of-20 at 0.0175, 0.3836 / 0-of-20 at 0.010, with ZERO escapes anywhere at r_eff >= 0.025. The naive 1-D strip binder 2*r_eff*L >= A_window predicts the cliff at 0.0110 m and is 2.3x too loose: area is not the binder, the last uncovered CELL is, and its distance to the contact polyline lies in (0.025, 0.0275] with the SAME value on fixture_A, fixture_B and fixture_R -- a property of the path and the scored window, not of the fixture. ESCAPE floor: the escape channel is non-empty for m <= 0.050 kg (2 residual escapes at 0.050, 20/11/15 of 20 at 0.045) and empty for m >= 0.055 kg, while coverage_cont is untouched (fixture_B 1.0000 at 0.045 kg) because success = (not escaped) and coverage_cont >= 0.90. The floor is set by the 20 Hz CONTROL TICK, not the integrator: N207's own criterion m >= K dt^2 = 0.0174 kg sits 2.9x below the last escaping mass and the servo-bandwidth form m >= K(TICK_S/2pi)^2 = 0.0633 kg sits 1.15x above the last clean one. An 8x rate (240 -> 1920 Hz) lifts the 0.030 kg arm only part of the way (fixture_B success 4/20 -> 10/20, coverage 0.6508 -> 0.6875, escapes 16 -> 8), so the floor is dynamics with a solver-dependent component. Q1 REFUTED (a square pad does NOT equate the rect and disc kernels -- rect - frozen = 0.0876/0.0938/0.0907 at r_eff 0.025, because the disc is inscribed and the gap is the pad's corner area, vanishing exactly at saturation 0.0000 for r_eff >= 0.0275). Q2 PARTLY CONFIRMED (every kernel saturates at 1.0000 at r_eff 0.035 for the square pad and for elongation along u or across v, max |delta| 0.0000) with the anisotropy REFUTED (elongation sign inconsistent: A +0.0104, B -0.0195, R +0.0144). Q3 REFUTED (N212's spacing law is not the binder here). Q5 CONFIRMED: the two modes fail through different channels -- every raster failure at a small pad is an ESCAPE, the trochoid loses coverage and stays escape-free. Q6 CONFIRMED: per-tool coverage_cont spread 0.0000, so decomposing the aliased tool axis costs nothing. rig keep=false in EVERY arm BY CONSTRUCTION and NO keep is claimed on the primary metric.

title: N215-FIXTURE-FACE-AXIS: validity audit of the FIXTURE FACE -- the tenth and last unvaried literal group. The face cliff is the commanded PLAN's own reach (0.0500 m on v), not patch+r_eff (refuted, 2.0x too tight), the loss channel is contact loss -> slide-off -> escape (a third channel), and the frozen face margins are 2.80x (v) / 1.51x (u) / 1.33x (round radius), so the pre-registered '1.27x across-patch face margin is the tightest term in the segment' is REFUTED
summary: Validity audit (new_mechanism=false) of the rig's FIXTURE-FACE axis, the last unvaried literal group after N207 rate, N208 iterations, N209 friction, N210 force, N211 kernel, N212 dose, N213 pose-noise and N214 tool body. _build_fixture hard-coded the two top faces (elongated box halfExtents [0.34, 0.14, 0.12], round cylinder radius 0.32) and tank_shape is a two-valued coin aliased with the seed, so 'Fixture-B zero-shot TRANSFER' was a claim about a geometry nobody had ever moved. Three absolute diagnostic knobs (AEGIS_FACE_HU_M / AEGIS_FACE_HV_M / AEGIS_FACE_R_M, all default 0.0 = the frozen literal) plus one face_half_extents() helper that _build_fixture and the orbit guard now share turn the face into a controlled dose: 40 arms, 4800 episodes, every arm paired in-rig on the SAME 20 seeds, identity arm bit-identical to Run350 (60/60 on coverage_cont/success/escaped/coverage/stall_frac/z_exc_max_m; max |d fn_mean| 0.1540 N = N210's cross-process force floor). THE LAW: the face must contain the COMMANDED PLAN's own excursion, not the scored patch plus the head's footprint. fixture_B (elongated) certifies 1.0000 / 20-20 / 0 escapes for every face_v in [0.0500, 0.140] (2.80x) and every face_u in [0.2250, 0.340] (1.51x); the v cliff is bracketed to (0.0475, 0.0500] and the u cliff to (0.2200, 0.2250], and those brackets CONTAIN the trochoid plan's own reaches measured from the rig's scrub_uv (v 0.0500, u 0.2230). F2 REFUTED in its stated falsification form: the pre-registered window patch_v + r_eff = [0.085, 0.100] is 2.0x above the measured cliff, and coverage collapses while face_v is BELOW the scored patch half-extent itself (0.050). The discriminator that separates 'plan reach' from 'patch half' is raster: its plan reaches only 0.0350 (1.43x inside the trochoid's) and ITS cliff moves with it, to (0.030, 0.040]. F1 CONFIRMED: order of first loss in fractional terms v 0.357 < u 0.662 < round radius 0.750. F3 REFUTED: the loss is not a graded contact-set shrink, it is a STEP with the escape test flipping 0 -> 20/20 (fixture_B face_v 0.0525 reads 1.0000 / 20-20 / 0 escapes / stall 0.000; face_v 0.0475 reads 0.2789 / 0-20 / 20 escapes / stall_frac 0.844 / launch_frac 0.0218). The channel is a THIRD one: the head loses contact, the lateral servo keeps driving it along the plan, it slides off the edge and trips the 0.60 m workspace escape test -- distinct from N213's launch-by-offset (launch_frac stays at 0.02) and from N214's mu*Fn slide-by-mass. F4 CONFIRMED: raster and trochoid fail in the same band (separation 0.010 = one ladder step) through the same channel (raster at 0.030: 13/20 escapes, stall_frac 0.672), and the one-step offset IS the difference between the two plans' reaches. F5 region CONFIRMED, second half REFUTED: the certificate is a region and the frozen face is NOT near its edge (2.80x / 1.51x / 1.33x), so the pre-registered 'the across-patch face margin is the tightest term in the whole segment, tighter than N214's 1.27x footprint floor and N214b's 1.45x mass floor' is refuted; the tightest FACE term is the round RADIUS at 1.33x, and the segment's tightest audited margin is still N214's footprint floor. Cliff SHARPNESS is a face-shape property: a flat edge PARALLEL to the plan's excursion gives a knife edge (exactly 1.0000 over a 2.80x band, then 0.279), a convex boundary the plan's corner crosses obliquely gives a graded ramp (round radius 1.000 / 0.937 / 0.881 / 0.867 / 0.831 / 0.480 at 0.240/0.230/0.225/0.220/0.215/0.200). The face budget is ADDITIVE with N213's term: at the responsive band (0.03,6) the same head drops to 0.6125 / 6-20 at face_v 0.060 and 0.5281 / 3-20 at 0.055, because face_half must cover plan_reach + the REALISED offset (N213: up to 3.63x the labelled sigma), so the face requirement is a shared budget, not a constant. rig keep=false in EVERY arm BY CONSTRUCTION and NO keep is claimed on the primary metric.
